nodes.title: Product goal
nodes.text: Build a polished, accessible Sudoku web app with Next.js and TypeScript. The first release is local-first: users can start a puzzle, enter and erase notes, receive validation feedback, pause, resume, and persist their current game without an account or backend.

nodes.title: MVP scope
nodes.text: Keep the first release focused on a dependable puzzle loop and a clear mobile experience.

rows: Puzzle modes

Select cell, enter digit, erase, notes, mistake feedback, completion state

Accounts, cloud sync, leaderboards

Responsive 9×9 grid, keypad, timer, pause, dark mode
Themes, animations, social sharing

Keyboard navigation, screen-reader labels, unit and browser tests
Native apps, offline install/PWA polish

nodes.title: Application architecture
nodes.text: Keep puzzle rules independent from React so correctness can be tested without a browser.

data.summary: The Next.js shell renders an accessible game surface around a pure Sudoku domain layer; persistence and puzzle generation stay behind small interfaces.

flow.detail: Client lifecycle, selection, input, timer, pause, announcements

components/SudokuGame.tsx — client boundary and orchestration

components/NumberPad.tsx — touch-friendly digit and erase controls

nodes.title: Technical contracts
nodes.text: Define the domain boundaries before UI polish so every visible state has one source of truth.

rows: Board state
Given cells, user values, notes, selected cell, status, elapsed time
Immutable or reducer-driven updates; givens are never editable
Validation
Row, column, box conflicts and completion checks
Validate against the active puzzle; do not mutate the board while checking
Candidates
Legal digits for a selected empty cell
Derive from row, column, and 3×3 box constraints
Generator
Create a solvable puzzle from a seed and difficulty
Verify unique solution before exposing a puzzle
Solver
Solve a complete candidate board deterministically
Keep it pure and bounded; never run in render
Persistence
Save and restore an in-progress game
Version snapshots and reject malformed or stale data
UI controller
Map input to domain actions and announcements
React state updates on semantic changes, not every timer tick

nodes.title: Phased implementation
nodes.text: Complete each phase only when its exit checks pass.

items.label: Phase 1 · Foundation
items.detail: Create the Next.js App Router app, TypeScript strictness, styling tokens, responsive shell, testing setup, and domain folder boundaries.

items.label: Phase 2 · Sudoku domain
items.detail: Implement board representation, givens, candidate calculation, conflict detection, completion rules, solver, seeded generation, and difficulty metadata.

items.label: Phase 3 · Playable grid
items.detail: Add the accessible 9×9 grid, selection model, keyboard navigation, digit/erase actions, notes mode, conflict highlighting, and number pad.

items.label: Phase 4 · Product loop
items.detail: Add new game flow, difficulty selection, timer, pause overlay, completion summary, mistake preference, and local save/resume.

items.label: Phase 5 · Resilience and polish
items.detail: Handle refresh and malformed storage, responsive layout, reduced motion, dark mode, focus restoration, announcements, and loading/error states.

items.label: Phase 6 · Verification and release
items.detail: Pass domain, component, browser, accessibility, responsive, and production-build gates; document deployment and known limits.

nodes.title: Delivery dependencies
nodes.text: The order reduces rewrite risk and keeps correctness ahead of visual polish.

nodes.title: Definition of done
nodes.text: The MVP is complete only when gameplay, accessibility, and resilience gates pass together.

items: Every shipped puzzle has exactly one solution and matches its declared difficulty band
Given cells cannot be edited or erased; user values and notes can be changed safely
Row, column, and box conflicts are visible and also announced through accessible status text
Keyboard users can move through all cells, enter digits, erase, toggle notes, pause, and restart
Touch users have large targets for digits, erase, notes, pause, and new game
Refresh restores the current puzzle, values, notes, timer, and preferences or safely starts clean
Completion is detected without requiring a server and shows an understandable summary
The layout works at narrow mobile widths without horizontal scrolling or clipped controls
Reduced-motion preference disables nonessential transitions and celebration effects
Unit tests cover solver correctness, uniqueness, candidates, conflicts, persistence migration, and completion
Playwright covers new game, input, notes, pause/resume, refresh restore, completion, and mobile viewport flows
Production build completes with no runtime console errors

nodes.title: Puzzle generation cost
nodes.text: Naive generation can create slow or inconsistent startup times, especially on mobile.

data.mitigation: Use seeded generation with bounded attempts, a deterministic solver, difficulty scoring, and precomputed fallback puzzles for each difficulty.

nodes.title: Accessibility of a 9×9 grid
nodes.text: A visually clear grid can still be confusing to keyboard and screen-reader users.

data.mitigation: Use a roving tabindex, explicit cell labels with row/column/value state, live announcements for conflicts and completion, and a non-color-only focus/peer highlight system.

nodes.title: Persistence corruption
nodes.text: Malformed or outdated localStorage can block the app or restore impossible state.

data.mitigation: Store a versioned schema, validate on read, migrate known versions, discard invalid snapshots safely, and expose a reset-game action.

nodes.title: Mobile input friction
nodes.text: A small keypad or dense board can cause accidental entries and loss of context.

data.mitigation: Use generous touch targets, a sticky number pad where appropriate, selected-cell emphasis, note mode feedback, and device-width browser testing.

nodes.title: Delivery risk map
nodes.text: Prioritize correctness and access before themes or celebration polish.

data.summary: Puzzle generation and grid accessibility are the highest-priority risks; persistence and mobile ergonomics need early validation.

nodes.title: Testing strategy
nodes.text: Use Vitest for pure Sudoku rules, solver/generator invariants, and persistence serialization. Use React Testing Library for selection, keyboard actions, number pad behavior, announcements, pause, and completion summary. Use Playwright for end-to-end new game, notes, invalid entries, refresh restore, mobile viewport, keyboard-only navigation, and a seeded completion fixture. Test at 320, 375, 768, and 1440 CSS pixels.

nodes.title: Explicit non-goals
nodes.text: Do not add authentication, databases, cloud sync, online multiplayer, social profiles, advertisements, complex state-management libraries, or an AI hint system in the MVP. Keep the first version local-first and make puzzle correctness measurable before adding engagement features.

nodes.title: Recommended delivery approach
nodes.text: Build a deterministic Sudoku domain first, then wrap it in an accessible client component. Use Next.js App Router for the shell and metadata, a narrow client boundary for interaction, a semantic grid for assistive technology, and localStorage behind a versioned adapter.

nodes.title: Implementation scope decision
nodes.text: Approve the local-first MVP plan before any app code is created.
